researched_by: the council's own traffic regulation orders on its Traffic Order Search portal, the consolidated order articles, an FOI disclosure, and town council papers
policy_summary:
SCOPE NOTE: Devon County Council is the highways authority for all of Devon except Plymouth and Torbay, which are unitary. It makes the on-street traffic regulation orders and runs civil parking enforcement on the highway. IT DOES NOT OWN THE CAR PARKS - those belong to the eight districts (East Devon, Exeter, Mid Devon, North Devon, South Hams, Teignbridge, Torridge, West Devon), and every off-street motorhome scheme in Devon is a district scheme, researched separately. Nothing in this file is about a car park.

There is NO county-wide Devon prohibition on overnight parking, on sleeping in a vehicle, or on motorhomes in lay-bys. Devon has not done what North Yorkshire did on its coast. What it has instead is a dedicated vehicle-class instrument: Schedule 14 of the Devon County Council (Traffic Regulation & On-Street Parking Places) Consolidation Order 2020, given effect by Article 8 - 'a Motor Caravan is not permitted to wait in a length of road contrary to the restrictions specified in the parts of schedule 14'. Motor caravan takes its meaning from the Motor Vehicles (Type Approval) (Great Britain) Regulations, so it is a BODY-TYPE test: it catches a DVLA-bodied motor caravan whether or not anyone is asleep in it, and it does not catch an unconverted panel van or a car camper.

Crucially the schedule restricts WAITING, not sleeping. Devon has created no offence of sleeping in a vehicle. If you are lawfully parked somewhere not listed in Schedule 14, DCC's orders do not make sleeping there unlawful.

Only two locations were found in Schedule 14, both coastal towns. EXMOUTH: the 2018 Exmouth Seafront (Prohibition of Motor Caravans) Amendment Order, in force 2 July 2018, banned motor caravans outright on stretches of Queen's Drive south side and banned them 8pm-8am on Imperial Road and the Queen's Drive Eastern Spur; a 12 May 2021 amendment restated this as 'No Motor Caravans At Any Time' on Queen's Drive and 'No Motor Caravans 8pm-8am' on Maer Road and the Eastern Spur. DARTMOUTH: the (South Hams) Amendment Order of 27 September 2019 prohibits motor caravans 6pm-midnight and midnight-9am on lengths of both North Embankment and South Embankment.

Exmouth is the case worth studying because it is a two-authority regime that actually works. DCC pushed motor caravans off the seafront highway; East Devon District Council took them in at Maer Road, Queen's Drive, Imperial Road Recreation Ground and the Estuary long-stay. Paid overnight stopovers rose from about 1,500 to 1,800 between April-August 2023 and the same window in 2024, and EDDC responded by capping stays at three nights. Restriction and provision arrived together, but from two different councils - which is why neither council's website tells you the whole story.
notes:
The most useful thing in this file is the shape of the instrument. Devon did not write a blanket. It wrote a named vehicle-class schedule and then added lengths of road to it one town at a time. That makes Devon's restrictions genuinely narrow - two towns in a county with hundreds of miles of coast - but also close to invisible, because nothing on a Devon council website says 'here is where motorhomes are banned'. You have to know Schedule 14 exists. The council's own TraffWeb mapping application does carry a 'Motor Caravan Prohibitions' legend layer, which is the authoritative mappable list and the right place for a human to go next.

Direction of travel: additive but slow, and stalled. Exmouth 2018, Dartmouth 2019, Exmouth tightened 2021, and then nothing new found through to 2026. Devon's motorhome pressure has not gone away; it has moved off the TRO track and onto two others - district car park pricing and night limits, and anti-social behaviour enforcement. Exmouth now funds ASB officers through the Police and Crime Commissioner to work evenings and weekends on loud music, fires and obstruction, with signage to match. That is a behavioural response, not a parking one, and it is what an authority reaches for when it does not want to make another order.

Enforcement reality is modest. DCC's FOI response on Exmouth seafront complaints identified 27 reports across three locations over three years. This is not a county under siege; it is two specific seafronts where residents complained loudly enough to get a schedule entry.

NO LAY-BY ORDER WAS FOUND. Searches for motorhome or overnight restrictions on the A39 Atlantic Highway, the A361 and A386 lay-bys returned nothing. Devon appears not to have used TROs on its A-road lay-bys against motorhomes at all. Absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence - but repeated searching found no such order.
open_questions: The FULL contents of Schedule 14. Sub-schedules 14.001, 14.002 (Exmouth) and 14.003, 14.004 (Dartmouth embankments) were identified from amendment orders. Whether any further entries exist elsewhere in Devon is unresolved. The 'Motor Caravan Prohibitions' layer in DCC's TraffWeb application (https://devon.traffweb.app/traffweb/1/TrafficOrders) is the definitive list and should be read directly.

The text of DCC's own guidance page 'Visiting Devon in your motor home' (https://www.devon.gov.uk/roads-and-transport/parking/visiting-devon-in-your-motor-home/) could NOT be retrieved - devon.gov.uk sits behind a JavaScript challenge and the host was unreachable by every route tried, including the Wayback Machine. This is the county-level policy statement and it has not been read. Someone should open it in a browser.

Whether the 12 May 2021 Exmouth order fully supersedes the 2018 hours. The 2018 order drafts the overnight ban as '8pm-midnight and midnight-8am'; the 2021 order says '8pm-8am'. Same practical effect, but the operative version should be confirmed.
Exact made and in-force dates for the Dartmouth amendment order. The document seal is undated in the published copy; 27 September 2019 comes from the related South Hams amendment order.
Whether any Devon lay-by carries an overnight or motor-caravan restriction at all, on the A39 or anywhere else.
Whether DCC has ever considered a county-wide overnight or coastal-corridor restriction. No committee paper proposing one was found.

sites.name: Queen's Drive, Exmouth (no motor caravans at any time)
sites.notes: Schedule 14.001. A 24-hour ban, not an overnight one: motor caravans may not wait at any time on four sections of the south side of Queen's Drive totalling about 219 metres, near the Queen's Drive Eastern Spur junction. Introduced by the Exmouth Seafront (Prohibition of Motor Caravans & Various Restrictions) Amendment Order 2018, made 18 June 2018 and in force 2 July 2018; restated as 'No Motor Caravans At Any Time' by the Queens Drive and Maer Road amendment order of 12 May 2021. Campervans can still use a pay-and-display area at the WESTERN end of the seafront. The restriction bites on body type, not on occupancy - it applies to an empty motor caravan at midday.
sites.geocode_precision: EX8 2AY postcode centroid on Queen's Drive; the restricted lengths run east of here towards the Eastern Spur junction

sites.name: Imperial Road, Maer Road and Queen's Drive Eastern Spur, Exmouth (no motor caravans overnight)
sites.search_hint: Imperial Road and Queen's Drive Eastern Spur, Exmouth
sites.notes: Schedule 14.002. The overnight limb of the Exmouth regime: no motor caravans 8pm-8am (drafted in the 2018 order as 8pm-midnight and midnight-8am) on about 94 metres of the east side of Imperial Road in three sections and about 558 metres of the south side of the Queen's Drive Eastern Spur in six sections, with Maer Road added by the 12 May 2021 amendment. Three streets across the seafront rather than a single place, so no single coordinate is honest here. The displaced traffic goes into East Devon District Council's Maer Road, Queen's Drive, Imperial Road Recreation Ground and Estuary car parks, which do permit overnight stays - capped at three nights since 2024.

sites.name: North Embankment and South Embankment, Dartmouth (no motor caravans overnight)
sites.notes: Schedules 14.003 and 14.004. Prohibition of motor caravans 6pm-midnight and midnight-9am on lengths of both embankments along the River Dart, introduced by the Devon County Council (Traffic Regulation & On-Street Parking Places) (South Hams) Amendment Order of 27 September 2019 and carried forward by the Various Streets, Dartmouth (Waiting Restrictions) Amendment Order. Five sections are listed on North Embankment alone, measured off the Lee Court property boundary and the College Way junction. The council's stated reason is to stop overnight camper van parking and the extended parking or storage of such vehicles on the waterfront. A wider overnight window than Exmouth's - it starts at 6pm and runs to 9am.
sites.geocode_precision: North Embankment street centre on the Dart waterfront; the restriction also covers South Embankment immediately to the south
